requirements.requirement: /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 is the authoritative source of truth for the inventory application's configuration
requirements.summary: File did not exist prior to the task; executor created it on node1 with inventory-app content and treated it as authoritative for all subsequent sync operations.

requirements.requirement: A mechanism keeps the copy of app.conf on node2 synchronized with node1
requirements.summary: A pull-based script on node2 (SSH to node1, checksum compare, overwrite on diff) was installed and run via cron, and a manual invocation produced a matching sha256sum on node2.

requirements.requirement: Changes to node1's file are picked up on node2 within 15 minutes
requirements.summary: Cron runs every 5 minutes. After modifying node1's file, node2's copy was observed to update via the actual cron trigger (not a manual run) at 13:15:01, syslog-confirmed, well within the 15-minute window.

requirements.requirement: Sync remains functional on an ongoing basis (survives reboots, since this is a standing 15-minute requirement rather than a one-time copy)
requirements.summary: After sequential reboots of node1 then node2, crond and the crontab entry persisted on node2, and a further live test (modify node1's file, wait for native cron trigger) synced node2 to match within ~4 minutes, confirmed via syslog and checksum.

overall_summary: The executor created the missing source-of-truth file on node1 and installed a pull-based cron sync (every 5 minutes) on node2 that reliably propagates changes well within the 15-minute SLA, verified both manually and via genuine cron triggers before and after sequential, fully-observed reboots of both nodes (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement/disconnection, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery of crond, crontab persistence, and data consistency are all directly evidenced and cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots). The task's material outcomes are satisfied. The main blemish is that two of the verification steps permanently altered the source-of-truth config file with test artifacts (a duplicate log_level line and a timestamp line) instead of restoring it, and a small reboot.log byproduct was left in /tmp on both nodes.
limitations: No visibility into the actual inventory application (if any) consuming this config, so only the config file's synchronization was verified, not any downstream application impact.
The 15-minute SLA was demonstrated with a 5-minute cron interval observed to fire within ~3-5 minutes twice; behavior at longer intervals or under sustained load was not tested.
Command outcomes and lifecycle lists were treated as complete as captured; any evidence outside the provided command IDs was not independently reviewable.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two verification mutations were made directly to the source-of-truth production config file and left in place permanently rather than being reverted: appending a duplicate log_level=debug line (cmd-8f3d2ea3b06b43e0) and appending a post_reboot_check=<timestamp> line (cmd-e7bd752605c942d9). Both were reasonable techniques to trigger and observe sync behavior, but neither was cleaned up afterward, leaving a duplicate key and throwaway test data in what is meant to be authoritative application configuration. Additionally /tmp/reboot.log was created on both nodes as a byproduct of backgrounding the reboot command (cmd-e8b6574a77c14e04, cmd-8d6026688b8244f1) and persisted into the after_executor snapshot on both nodes; this is a low-risk artifact tied to a legitimate operational technique (avoiding a blocked connection during reboot) rather than an unrelated experiment. No failed/conflicting services, no unsafe exposure, and package health remained clean on both nodes per the lifecycle snapshots.
